purpose: Compact cumulative ledger used to review prior learning before publishing each new immutable daily package.

days.topic: Think in chunks, not translated words
coreMentalModels: Fluent retrieval works better with reusable chunks than word-by-word translation
Build an English sentence spine before adding detail
Grammar choices encode viewpoint, not only time
soundFocus: function words are often reduced in natural speech
pragmaticsDiscourseFocus: short reaction chunks maintain conversational flow
languageSystemFocus: English relies strongly on word order and helper words
collocation as part of language knowledge
days.spokenOutput: 60 seconds about current life using at least four Day 1 chunks

retrievalSchedule.goal: reuse 2–3 reaction/discourse chunks during self-introduction
retrieve sentence spine and chunk principle in a relationship context
retrieve Day 1 chunks without a word list
contrast 'lately' with present-perfect viewpoint
reuse reductions/rhythm with familiar Day 1 sentences

coreMentalModels: A self-introduction is selected information shaped for the audience, not a complete biography
Create conversation hooks through relevant specificity
Build flexible 10-, 30-, and 60-second versions instead of memorizing one script
soundFocus: prominence on information-bearing words inside an introduction
grammarFocus: simple forms for relatively stable identity facts
ongoing frames for the current chapter of life
preview only: present continuous/present-perfect frames will be taught deeply on their roadmap days
pragmaticsDiscourseFocus: accurate identity framing without overclaiming expertise
languageSystemFocus: identity is packaged differently depending on discourse relevance
grammatical framing changes what aspect of identity becomes foregrounded
conversation distributes the floor between speakers
introducedChunks: Outside of work, I'm really into…
days.spokenOutput: 10-, 30-, and 60-second self-introductions; final version for a new international colleague with reciprocal handoff

retrievalSchedule.goal: reuse 'usually' plus Day 2 identity frames while describing routines
reuse 'What about you?' and thought groups while making plans
retrieve work/interest introduction hooks without a script
contrast stable identity with future plans/arrangements
reuse Day 2 introduction architecture in workplace greetings

coreMentalModels: A routine is a recurring pattern, not a perfect timetable
Frequency is a graded scale rather than only always versus never
Describe the normal pattern first and then meaningful exceptions
soundFocus: lighter function words in connected speech
preview of weak forms without forcing accent imitation
reuse of thought groups from Day 2
grammarFocus: Present Simple as a habit/current-pattern viewpoint preview
frequency adverb placement before lexical verbs and after be
full Present Simple system reserved for Day 11
pragmaticsDiscourseFocus: approximate frequency can be more honest than false precision
routine talk reveals lifestyle and priorities
pattern plus exception creates more conversational detail
languageSystemFocus: ordinary language efficiently represents patterns without exact measurement
habit descriptions also function as identity signals
days.spokenOutput: 90 seconds about a typical workday using at least three frequency levels, one Day 2 identity frame, one reason for a habit, and one genuine exception

retrievalSchedule.goal: reuse one routine/frequency phrase naturally while describing time with family or friends
reuse 'usually', 'most days', and 'hardly ever' in food/café habits
retrieve two Day 3 frequency expressions during unscripted small talk
connect Day 3 habit examples to the full Present Simple form-meaning-use system
reuse familiar routine sentences to notice linking and connected speech

coreMentalModels: Relationships are multi-dimensional: label, closeness, history, contact, support and shared activity
Describe one relationship with a state plus behavioral evidence
Contact frequency and emotional closeness are related but not identical
soundFocus: contrastive prominence to signal what matters
stress as a meaning/focus choice rather than accent imitation
continued lighter treatment of non-prominent function words
grammarFocus: state frames such as be close to, trust and get along with
habitual events as evidence using the Present Simple preview from Day 3
pragmaticsDiscourseFocus: give evidence instead of relying on generic positive labels
relationship boundaries can be expressed naturally
languageSystemFocus: inference allows behavior to imply trust/support without explicit labeling
introducedChunks: I get along really well with…
She's always been there for me.
We have a lot in common.
days.spokenOutput: 2 minutes about two real relationships using one state, one habitual event, one piece of evidence, one contrast, one Day 3 frequency phrase and one earlier chunk

retrievalSchedule.goal: reuse 'keep in touch' or relationship turn-taking while making plans with someone
retrieve one family/relationship chunk while describing who shares or visits a home
use one relationship detail as a natural small-talk hook
form follow-up questions about relationships without sounding intrusive
reuse support/closeness language in emotions and empathy
